sec: ADA 2024 drug combinations and insulin indications

items.q: Match the following indication — 1) HbA1c ≥1.5–2% above target 2) Glycaemic triad / ketosis 3) Pregnancy hyperglycaemia 4) Vascular complications … A) Dual therapy initially B) Insulin C) Insulin (gestational / T1DM) D) Insulin after failure of dual therapy
items.exp: HbA1c significantly above target warrants dual therapy; ketosis prompts insulin; pregnancy hyperglycaemia needs insulin; vascular complications are not themselves an indication for insulin but guide agent choice. (Book p934)

items.q: A patient with new T2DM has HbA1c 10.2%, BMI 31 and no contraindications. The ADA 2024 approach is most consistent with:
opts: Initial dual therapy (metformin + GLP-1 RA or SGLT2i)
items.exp: HbA1c ≥1.5–2% above target (HbA1c 10.2% vs 7% target) warrants initial dual therapy or combination injectable therapy. (Book p934)

items.q: Assess insulin indications: I Insulin is mandatory in type 1 diabetes. II Insulin is preferred in pregnancy with hyperglycaemia.
items.exp: Insulin is the only approved therapy for Type 1 diabetes and the preferred agent in pregnancy when glycaemia is uncontrolled. (Book p934)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a non-insulin agent with proven cardiovascular benefit?
items.exp: Gliclazide has cardiovascular safety data but not the same mortality benefit as SGLT2i and GLP-1 RAs. (Book p934)

items.q: ADA 2024 recommends initiating ___ therapy in patients with HbA1c ≥1.5% above target.
items.exp: Dual therapy is recommended when HbA1c is ≥1.5% above target to accelerate glycaemic control. (Book p934)

items.q: Match the following agent to its specific trial / indication — 1) Empagliflozin 2) Liraglutide 3) Canagliflozin 4) Dapagliflozin … A) EMPA-REG (CV + renal) B) LEADER (CV) C) CREDENCE (renal) D) DAPA-HF (HF, non-diabetic included)
items.exp: EMPA-REG (empagliflozin, CV + renal); LEADER (liraglutide, CV); CREDENCE (canagliflozin, renal); DAPA-HF (dapagliflozin, HF including non-DM). (Book p934)

items.q: A patient with T2DM and HFpEF is on metformin; the clinician considers adding an SGLT2i for HF hospitalisation benefit. The most appropriate choice is:
items.exp: Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin reduce HF hospitalisation in HF regardless of ejection fraction; saxagliptin has increased HF risk; pioglitazone worsens HF. (Book p934)

items.q: Assess saxagliptin: I Saxagliptin is associated with increased HF hospitalisation. II It is the preferred DPP-4 inhibitor in HF.
items.exp: SAVOR-TIMI-53 showed increased HF hospitalisation with saxagliptin; it is not preferred in HF. (Book p934)

items.q: Match the following combination to its rationale — 1) Metformin + GLP-1 RA 2) Metformin + SGLT2i 3) GLP-1 RA + basal insulin 4) Metformin + TZD … A) Glycaemia + weight loss + CV benefit B) Glycaemia + cardio-renal + HF benefit C) Glycaemia with low hypoglycaemia D) Glycaemia + insulin sensitisation (watch for HF)
items.exp: Metformin + GLP-1 RA gives CV benefit; metformin + SGLT2i gives cardio-renal + HF benefit; GLP-1 + basal insulin gives low hypo; metformin + TZD sensitises with HF caution. (Book p934)

items.q: A patient with T2DM on metformin and liraglutide needs further glycaemic control. The most appropriate add-on with cardio-renal benefit is:
items.exp: Adding an SGLT2 inhibitor provides additional cardio-renal benefit without much hypoglycaemia risk. (Book p934)

items.q: Insulin should be initiated in T2DM if there is ___, HbA1c ≥10%, or features of the glycaemic triad.
items.exp: Insulin is added when combination oral / injectable therapy fails to control glycaemia, especially with severe hyperglycaemia or ketosis. (Book p934)

items.q: Assess insulin timing: I Basal insulin is preferred over premixed in T2DM. II Basal insulin can be combined with GLP-1 RA.
items.exp: Basal insulin is preferred for simplicity and lower hypo risk; iDegLira and iGlarLixi are fixed-ratio combinations with GLP-1 RA / GIP. (Book p934)
